2027 Aviva Technology & Change Delivery Graduate Pathway
Location: United Kingdom
Salary: £34,200
Closes: 01 December 2026
 Apply Now  Email this Job
In Summary
Do you enjoy bringing people together, solving problems and making things happen? If so, our Technology & Change Delivery pathway could be perfect for you!
Job Description
Locations: Bristol, Norwich, York, London
Hours: Full time, permanent with two-year development programme
Work type: Hybrid
Salary: £34,200

The opportunity

If you're naturally curious, enjoy solving problems and like finding better ways of doing things, Change Delivery could be for you. You'll help shape and deliver improvements that make a real difference for our customers and colleagues. Whether that's bringing people together, analysing information, improving processes or using technology to solve business challenges, you'll play a key role in driving change across Aviva.

You don't need to be a technology expert, just someone who enjoys learning, seeing the bigger picture and turning ideas into action.

Whatever path you choose, you'll work on live projects, learn from experienced colleagues and help deliver even better experiences for millions of customers.   

“Everyone I’ve worked with at Aviva has been incredibly supportive and welcoming. There’s a real emphasis on learning and development, which makes it a great place to start your career. I’ve been able to develop both my technical knowledge and my confidence in working with a wide range of people across the business.”Current Graduate  

The roles
Our Technology Change Delivery roles are based in Bristol, Norwich, York and London. You may need to be flexible on location and willing to relocate if needed. We believe some of the best collaboration, learning, and relationship building happens when people come together in-person. That's why our colleagues spend around 50% or more of their working time in the office. We call this Smart Working. For most colleagues, that means spending around three days a week in the office and the rest working from home, although this varies by role and team.

Solution Architect (Bristol, Norwich, York) - you'll help shape how our business uses data and technology to solve real business problems. Working with teams across the business, you'll design solutions, recommend the right tools and help turn complex ideas into practical outcomes. Whether that's improving how data is shared, supporting the adoption of new technologies or creating smarter ways of working, you'll play a key role in helping us make better decisions for our customers and our business.

Project Manager (Norwich)- you'll help turn ideas into action, bringing together the right people to deliver change that makes a real difference for our customers. You'll keep projects moving forward, coordinate teams and solve problems when challenges arise. Whether that's removing blockers, managing risks, keeping plans on track or improving the way we work, you'll play a key role in delivering successful outcomes. Working with colleagues, suppliers and partners, you'll help make sure everyone is aligned, informed and focused on what's most important.

Business Analyst (Norwich)- you’ll help uncover what customers really need and work with teams to deliver practical solutions. You’ll ask insightful questions and challenge assumptions to identify opportunities for improvement. Whether that’s analysing data, solving problems, maximising opportunities, removing blockers, or shaping smarter ways of working, you’ll play a key role in helping us do things better: for our customers, our business, and your own development.

Executive and Events IT Support (London): you'll help keep people connected, productive and supported through great technology. Working with colleagues across the business, including senior leaders, you'll provide hands-on IT support, troubleshoot technical issues and help deliver seamless technology experiences. From supporting high-profile events and live broadcasts to helping colleagues get the most from their technology, no two days are the same. If you enjoy solving problems, building relationships and working with technology, you'll play an important role in helping Aviva operate at its best.

Cyber Security (Bristol): you'll help protect Aviva's systems, data and customers from cyber threats. Working with experienced security professionals, you'll support activities that identify risks, strengthen security controls and help keep our technology safe and secure. From monitoring potential threats and investigating security issues to supporting colleagues and promoting good security practices, you'll play an important role in protecting our business. If you're curious, analytical and interested in how technology can be used to manage risk and defend against emerging threats, this could be the role for you. 



 
About Us
The company

We help millions of customers across the UK, Ireland and Canada protect what matters most to them and plan for their future. Whether it's supporting someone after an accident, helping families feel financially secure, or finding better ways to prepare for tomorrow, our work has a real impact on people's lives.

But we're not just here to solve today's challenges. We’re also investing in technology, data and AI to transform the way we work and deliver even better experiences for our customers.

For you, that means the opportunity to be part of a business that's constantly evolving, bringing fresh ideas to life and making a real difference to millions of people every day.

The Early Careers Development Programme

From day one, you'll become part of a community of graduates and apprentices from across the business.  During your first two years with us, alongside your day job, you'll take part in our Early Careers Development Programme.

Designed to complement your on-the-job learning, it combines structured development, networking and hands-on experiences to help you broaden your perspective and connect with people from across the business.

You'll learn alongside other graduates and apprentices, gain exposure to senior leaders and develop a broader understanding of the business.

What we’re looking for
You'll already have, or be on track to achieve, a degree in any subject by the end of summer 2027 and be ready to start your career with us full-time in September 2027. As well as being:

a strong communicator
curious about emerging technologies and keen to learn
a confident problem solver, passionate about helping others
analytical and logical in your thinking.  

Visa sponsorship is not available.To apply, you’ll need indefinite right to work in the UK.  If this applies to you, we’d love to hear from you

 
Additional Information
What you’ll get

£34,200 salary, plus discretionary bonus, employee discounts and access to our Share Save scheme
29 days' holiday plus bank holidays
Flexible working, wellbeing support and paid volunteering days, helping you maintain a healthy work-life balance 
A two-year Early Careers Development Programme, helping you build the skills, confidence and connections to succeed in your career  


How to apply
Our applications close on 1 December 2026. If we receive lots of great applications, we may close them sooner, so we’d encourage you to apply early. You can only apply for one pathway, so take some time to explore your options and choose the one that best matches your interests and strengths.
You'll be able to tell us if you need any additional support or reasonable adjustments during your online application.  
Each stage of our application process is designed to bring out the best in you. Below is a step-by-step guide on what to expect for each pathway.  

Online application
Online situational strengths and numerical reasoning tests
Video interview and AI literacy assessment
Virtual assessment day          

You’ll meet some of the team, get a feel for what it’s like to work here and show us what you’re all about. If you’re successful, you’ll get an offer to start in September 2027.   

We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives because we know diverse teams make us stronger. 

We're interested in people with potential, curiosity and a willingness to learn. So, if you're excited by the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.

Open Date: 14 October 2026
Date Added: 14 October 2026

Cyber Security Summer Internship, Warwick
About the Position
Our IT & Digital function is using new and disruptive technologies to help improve how we do our job – through cloud computing, artificial intelligence or machine learning to name just a few. From IT support to data, security to new technologies, we partner with the business to achieve our overall vision to be at the heart of a clean, fair and affordable energy future.

Within IT&D, our Security team protect our people, premises and digital systems with the objective of maintaining trust in National Grid’s services. Our work includes reducing technology risks, building secure systems, meeting legal requirements, preventing and responding to cyberattacks, investigating incidents, training employees and planning future security improvements. If defending IT infrastructure and networks or combating cyber-crimes appeals, then starting a career in cyber security is for you.

The services underpinning digital security are wide-ranging. You could make your mark in:

Business Partnering – Develop improvement plans to effectively manage our technology risk profile in line with our strategic objectives. Ensure that our products are secure by design. Keep our businesses compliant with regulation and manage the demand for centralised cyber services via prioritisation of requirements.
Cyber Security Strategy, Engineering and Architecture – plan, design, implement and support effective cyber security solutions, including network & email, identity & access management, cloud & data security
Operations – protect, detect and respond to cyber incidents, provide specialist digital forensic support, manage vulnerabilities and analyse threat intelligence.
Office of the CISO – define strategy and report security performance, provide training and awareness for the wider business to strengthen our ‘human firewall’, manage financial performance and investment, develop our people for success.
What You'll Do
As a Cyber Security Summer Intern, you'll gain hands-on experience working alongside experts who help protect National Grid's people, data and critical infrastructure. You'll contribute to real projects, develop your technical understanding and gain insight into how cyber security is managed across a large, regulated organisation.
Across the 12 week placement you'll gain experience in some of the following:
Risk Assessment & Mitigation: Analyse potential security risks and collaborate across departments to implement measures that reduce exposure.
Policy Implementation & Incident Planning: Support the rollout of security policies and develop plans to respond effectively to security incidents.
Testing & Investigation: Conduct system tests to identify vulnerabilities, maintain detailed investigation records, and report findings.
Reporting & Strategy Support: Prepare technical reports to inform strategic decisions and recommend upgrades or remediation actions.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with IT and other teams to ensure security risks are addressed and managed effectively.
What You'll Need to Apply
You’ll need to be in your penultimate year and expecting to achieve a minimum 2.2 degree in a Cyber Security degree or a degree with a significant amount of Cyber Security content (and be able to provide evidence of this) such as a computer science degree.

This role is subject to National Security Vetting (NSV) at Security Check (SC) level in addition to our standard background checks. You must hold, or be eligible to hold, a valid British passport and meet the minimum residency requirement of having lived continuously in the UK for the previous five years. We encourage applications from candidates who meet the essential qualification requirements and are prepared to undergo and maintain the necessary security clearance throughout their employment. Full GOV.UK Guidance can be found here.

Location
This role is based in National Grid House, Warwick and may offer flexible hybrid working, where possible. You'll be expected attend and work from your office location regularly.

What You'll Get In Return
We are proud to offer a salary of £25,946 (pro rata) for the duration of your 12 week Summer Internship.

As a first step in your career within the energy industry, our Summer Internship offers a unique opportunity to develop your skills, gain valuable experience, and gain insight into what a career with National Grid can offer.

Alongside a tailored development programme, you'll also enjoy a range of fantastic rewards and benefits, including:

Meaningful, hands-on experience working on real projects that contribute to the future of energy.
The opportunity to develop valuable professional, technical and leadership skills.
A dedicated support network, including mentorship, regular feedback and guidance from experienced colleagues.
26 days' annual leave (pro-rated where applicable), plus statutory holidays.
The opportunity to participate in our employee wellbeing programmes and initiatives.
You’ll gain more than just experience. We believe in nurturing talent and recognising exceptional performance. If you excel during your placement, you may receive an offer to join our Graduate Programme after you successfully complete your degree.

About our Summer Internship Programme
Our 12-week Summer Internship offers you the opportunity to kickstart your career within the energy sector. Throughout your placement, you’ll receive a tailored development programme designed to support your growth and development. This includes a combination of in-person and virtual training sessions led by our development team, as well as access to a range digital learning tools to help further enhance your skills.

Throughout your placement you’ll have opportunity to make connections amongst your cohort as well as regular check ins with a mentor and our Early Careers Team. Day-to-day, your placement manager will provide you access to a variety of on-the-job opportunities where you’ll take on real assignments and projects to make a genuine impact within your respective function. By the end of your placement, you’ll have developed your understanding of our business and the energy sector for your future career.

About National Grid
National Grid is the UK’s critical energy infrastructure company, operating the electricity network and infrastructure that connects millions of people to the energy they use every day, supporting homes, businesses and communities across England and Wales.

We know the future of energy won't be shaped by what we know today. It will be shaped by what's possible tomorrow. That's why we're investing in the next generation of talent, giving apprentices, undergraduates and graduates the opportunity to learn from experts, gain hands-on experience and contribute to work that matters from day one.

Are you ready to unlock the power of the possible?

More Information
You can apply for only one opportunity across all Early Careers and Career Changer programmes. Before applying, please carefully review all available programmes and choose the one that best matches your interests and career goals.
We recruit on a rolling basis across our Early Careers Roles. We may close our vacancies early once we have enough applications. We therefore encourage you to apply as early as possible.

National Grid's Early Careers opportunities in the UK are open to all applicants who meet the eligibility criteria including an existing and valid right to work in the UK. As part of the application process this will need to be evidenced and verified before you can start the programme.

Please note that in most cases, National Grid is unable to offer sponsorship for employment under the UK points-based immigration system. As such, applicants must have the legal right to work in the UK without requiring sponsorship now or in the future under the UK points-based immigration system. However, in exceptional circumstances where there is a clear and demonstrable need for specialist skills that cannot be sourced from the local labour market, National Grid may consider offering sponsorship. All applications are welcome from candidates who meet these requirements, regardless of race, nationality, or ethnic origin.

Please be aware that it’s your responsibility to explore avenues of working in the UK, as we're not able to provide advice on this. For information about visas please visit https://www.gov.uk/browse/visas-immigration/work-visas

Company Description
At Frasers Group we’re rethinking retail. Through digital innovation and unique store experiences, we’re serving our consumers with the world’s best sports, premium and luxury brands globally. As a leader in the industry, we’re elevating the retail experience for our consumers through our collection of established brands, including Sports Direct, FLANNELS, USC, Frasers, and GAME.

Why join us?

Our vision - We are building the planet’s most admired and compelling brand ecosystem

Our purpose - We are elevating the lives of the many with access to the world’s best brands and experiences

At Frasers Group, we fear less and do more. Our people are forward thinkers who are driven to operate outside of their comfort zone to change the future of retail, embracing challenges along the way.
